full_judgment:
3.The prosecution case, in brief, is that complainant's elder brother Alam Hasant Md Golam Rabbani served under the Government of Iraq in Al-Qut Cotton Mill and died in Gulf War in 1991 and that a compensation of US$ amounting to 1,00,000 was allotted to the heirs of deceased Alam Hasnat Md. Golam Rabbani. The complainant was pressing the Janashakti Karma Sangsthan-o-Proshikhan Bureau, Dhaka for getting compensation money and he was told that an amount 2,500 US dollar had been allotted. The complainant received the said amount from the aforesaid office. Later the complainant came to know that the remaining amount of US $ 97,500 had been misappropriated by the officers (accused-appellants) and, as such, the complainant filed a criminal case being Special Case No.68 of 2003 under sections 406/409/420/460 and 469 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 before the learned Senior Special Judge, Dhaka. The learned Judge after examining the complainant and hearing the order dated 31-7-2003 directed to write to the proper authority for obtaining sanction against the accused-petitioners. A letter from the Prime Minister's Secretariat dated 31-8-2003 was received by the learned Special Judge intimating that the matter of according sanction was under consideration. After that, by a memo dated 03-11-2003, the Director of the Prime Minister's Secretariat intimated about refusal of according sanction to prosecute the accused-petitioners. On perusal of the aforesaid letter of the Prime Minister's Secretariat dated 3-11-2003, the learned Special Judge by the order dated 26-10-2005 filed (নথিভুক্ত) the case. 

 6. Mr TH Khan, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the Prime Minister's Secretariat refused to accord sanction within 56 working days of the receipt of the letter from the Court of the Special Judge and that the High Court Division without looking into this broad fact came to a finding that since the sanction was refused beyond 60 days it would be deemed that sanction had been accorded and, as such, the impugned judgment should be set-aside. He further submits that the investigation report and the important correspondences that took place between relevant branches of the Government and the United Nations Compensation Commission (UNCC) and that some of the relevant correspondences have been incorporated in the additional paper book and that this correspondences clearly established that complainant's brother Md. Alam Hasnat Md. Golam Rabbani was sanctioned only an amount of US $ 2,500 according to the categorization made by the UNCC and, as such, the impugned judgment should be set-aside. He further submits that from the correspondences made with the UNCC by the relevant branches of the Government, it appears that the complainant's imaginary claim of US$ 100,000 was not true and that these correspondences could not be produced before the High Court Division as no notice was served upon the present appellants and, as such, the impugned judgment should be set-aside. 

 "The learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in misinterpreting and misconstruing provisions of section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 overlooking the main purpose and spirit of the provision of sanction provided in the said section; that the reason behind according sanction is to protect public officers from frivolous and vexatious prosecution and unnecessary harassment and that being so 'Sanction' does not mean just a formal paper transaction; that a duty has been cast upon the concerned sanction giving authority to examine the allegation and this necessarily involves investigation, which may take a couple of days to complete or it may take couple of months, according to the varying circumstances of each case, but the learned Judges of the High Court Division overlooked this aspect of the case and put erroneous construction on the deeming clause of 60 days, thinking, as if, the concerned authority was 'sleeping' over the learned Special Judge's letter dated 24-8-2003 received on 27-8-2003, which is far from the actual situation and that having regard to the facts and circumstances of the instant case viz-a-viz, the huge amount claimed by the complainant Kayser Parvez, it became incumbent upon the concerned sanction giving authority to hold an investigation as to the veracity of the claim and this was actually done and as a matter of fact the authority by its letter dated 31-8-2003 informed the court that the matter was under consideration of the Government and the decision would be intimated soon; that this vital fact makes all difference and distinguishes the present case from all other cases; that the learned Judges decision overlooking this vital aspect has vitiated the decision as a whole and the petitioners have been gravely prejudiced thereby. No notice of the Criminal Revision No. 244 of 2005 was served upon the present petitioners; consequently they could not contest the case and could not place the full facts including the investigation report and important correspondence that took place between the relevant branches of the Government and the United Nations Compensation Commission (UNCC): some of the relevant correspondence have been incorporated in an additional paper book with an application sworn on 30-3-2006; that these correspondence clearly establish that the complaint's brother Hasnat Golam Rabbani was sanctioned only an amount of US $ 2,500 only and not a penny more, according to the categorization made by the UNCC and thus the documents disproved the complainant Kaisar Pervez's imaginary claim that United Nations allowed 1,00,000 US$ and equal amount was given by the Iraq Government as compensation for his deceased brother. The deeming Clause of 60 days is to be interpreted taking into consideration of the factual aspects, but this was not been done in the present case resulting in miscarriage of justice and harassment." 

 10. On 31-7-2003, respondent No.1 Md Kayser Parvej (Milon) filed a petition of complaint before the Metropolitan Special Judge, Dhaka against the present appellants and another under sections 406/409/420/460 and 469 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 stating that his brother Md Alam Hasnat Md Golam Rabbani died in Gulf war in 1991. He alleged that the UNCC allocated a sum of US $ 100,000 but only US. $ 2500 was paid and the remaining US $ 97509 was misappropriated by the appellants and another. On 31-7-2003, learned Special Judge, passed an order to write a letter to accord sanction from proper authority and fixed the next date on 24-8-2003 for sanction. On 24-8-2003 the said letter seeking sanction was issued. On 27-8-2003, the Prime Minister's Secretariat received the said letter. On 31-8-2003, the Prime Minister's Secretariat by a memo informed the Court that the matter relating to granting sanction was under consideration and the decision would soon be communicated. On 3-11-2003, the Prime Minister's Secretariat by a memo informed the Court that the Government decided not to accord sanction against the appellants. On 26-1-2005, the learned Special Judge ordered the case to be filed since no sanction was accorded by the Government. 

 12. Relying upon the proviso to section 6(5) of the Criminal Amendment Act, 1958 (Act XL of 1958), the High Court Division came to a finding that since the decision of the Government not to accord sanction against the appellants was not given within 60 days, it would be deemed that sanction had been accorded. 

 13. It is contended that the Government's decision not to accord sanction was given within 56 working days of the receipt of the letter by the Secretariat of the Prime Minister. 

 14. Having gone through the materials on record, we find that on 27-8-2003, the letter seeking sanction was obtained by the Prime Minister's Secretariat. On 3-11-2003, the Prime Minister's Secretariat by a memo informed the Court that the Government decided not to accord sanction against the appellants. From 27-8-2003 to 3-11-2003 more than 60 days had elapsed. The words "working days" have not been mentioned in the proviso to section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. Therefore, the High Court Division was justified in holding that since the Government's decision not to-accord sanction against the appellants was intimated beyond 60 days, it would be deemed that sanction had been accorded according to the proviso to section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. 

 16. It is contended that the appellants could not produce the correspondences between the relevant branches of the Government and the UNCC before the High Court Division as no notice was served upon appellants. 

 19. We have gone through the investigation report and the important correspondences that took place between the different branches of the Government and UNCC. Some of the correspondences were incorporated in the additional paper book. The correspondences clearly establish that the complainant's brother Alam Hasant Md. Golam Rabbani was sanctioned only an amount of U.S.$ 2500 and not a cent more according to the categorization made by the UNCC. The complainant Kayser Parvej's imaginary claim that United Nations allowed US $ 100,000 and equal amount was given by the Iraq Government as compensation for his deceased brother is not true.
